message:
Plain words: the weight budget now names every part so the 60 kg limit check is auditable, Manager. The named mass sum (E68) totals 46.0 kg against 60.0 kg leaving 14.0 kg margin, about a carry-on bag spare on a person-scale machine, so Power Structure and Integration Lead recomputed it to list frame, wheels, chains, hopper, discharge, battery, avionics and harness rather than reuse the unnamed total.

Plain words: Autonomy and Blind Operations Lead stall protection and Mobility and Deployable Chassis Lead tip rule size my power and structure branches, Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead please note. I take from the Systems, devices, and/or methods regarding excavating (E57) and its patent twin (E56) the finding that an excavator backs crowd motion off on detected hoist-motor stall, which for this device means the ladder driver must be a current-limited fused branch that folds back before the fuse blows; I take from the Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) the rule that a raised load transfers weight and raises the Centre of Gravity (CG, meaning balance point), which for this device means the rear pivot lugs plus tilt motor carry 15.0 kg soil plus steel at 0.550 m pivot clearing the 0.400 m lip from the tip dump clearance check (E51).

Plain words: the power path stays continuous from battery to loads with no hidden break. Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, meaning safe long-life rechargeable chemistry) 24 V 20 Ah holds 480 Wh against dig 16.4 W from the ladder power estimate (E59) and 0.512 Wh per 15 kg trip from the dig energy estimate (E60), everyday scale a small bulb for two minutes against a household daily thousand Wh, with sag 3.96 mm from the stiffened sag estimate (E63) holding millimetre stiffness. Ready, because named mass, fused current-limited bus and level-gated pivot load now survive my strongest power-structure objections, leaving only arching, wear and fiducial bench tests.
